item.title: [PBV7-486] Implement the WebSocket protocol and Redis messaging layer
item.description:
Source and parent

Specification: Realtime WebSocket Platform – .NET 10, Redis, and Kubernetes
Parent Epic: PBV7-484

Context

Implement the application behavior that replaces SignalR conveniences with an explicit, testable protocol and enables horizontal fan-out through Redis while retaining local ownership of live WebSocket objects.

Requirements

  • Implement the WebSocket endpoint, local connection registry, connection context, dispatcher, topic/group routing, heartbeat, idle detection, graceful drain, and structured close behavior.
  • Define versioned message envelopes for client commands, server events, acknowledgments, correlation IDs, timestamps, payloads, and structured errors.
  • Enforce maximum frame and assembled-message sizes.
  • Use bounded per-connection outbound queues and define backpressure, dropped-message, and slow-consumer behavior.
  • Implement client reconnect guidance with exponential backoff, jitter, and service-restart handling.
  • Validate same-origin HttpOnly session cookies against the existing Redis session contract.
  • Validate the Origin header against an explicit allowlist.
  • Support short-lived, single-use Redis-backed connection tickets for approved cross-origin or non-browser clients.
  • Authorize every command and subscription using server-derived tenant and identity scope.
  • Implement namespaced Redis Pub/Sub fan-out across gateway instances.
  • Implement optional Redis Streams support only for approved durable/replay event classes, including retention, acknowledgment, pending-entry recovery, idempotency, and poison-message behavior.
  • Keep WebSocket objects local; do not store them in Redis.
  • Instrument connections, messages, queues, handlers, authentication, authorization, Redis, close codes, and drain behavior with Prometheus-compatible metrics and trace correlation.
  • Document the wire protocol, authentication flows, authorization boundaries, delivery semantics, error contract, reconnect behavior, and compatibility policy.

Dependencies

  • Standalone solution foundation.
  • Existing Redis session schema and validation contract.
  • Approved event classes and their delivery requirements.

Completion criteria

  • Two gateway instances exchange authorized events through Redis Pub/Sub.
  • A reconnect may land on another instance and successfully revalidate the session.
  • Tenant and user isolation is enforced for every routed message.
  • Queue bounds prevent a slow client from causing unbounded memory growth.
  • Pub/Sub and Streams semantics are explicit and not interchangeable.
  • Redis reconnect behavior does not corrupt local connection state.
  • Protocol and security documentation completes technical review.

Testing criteria

  • Unit-test protocol serialization, version compatibility, validation, authorization, and error frames.
  • Test valid, expired, missing, reused, and unauthorized session or connection-ticket cases.
  • Test allowed and rejected Origin values.
  • Test cross-tenant and cross-user subscription attempts.
  • Test malformed frames, oversized frames, fragmented messages, unsupported message types, and duplicate correlation IDs.
  • Test heartbeat timeout, abrupt disconnect, graceful drain, and client reconnect.
  • Run a two-instance Redis integration test in which a client connected to one instance receives an event published through another.
  • Interrupt and restore Redis and verify bounded retry, health state, metrics, logs, and recovery.
  • Test queue saturation, backpressure, dropped-message metrics, and slow-consumer disconnection.
  • Where Streams is enabled, test acknowledgment, replay, retention, duplicate delivery, consumer recovery, and pending-entry reassignment.
  • Confirm logs, metrics, and traces do not expose cookies, tokens, payload secrets, or unrestricted tenant identifiers.
